complexity.notes: Storing d[None] = None is a neat trick that lets the second pass assign pointers without null checks. Nodes are keyed by identity (the class defines no __hash__/__eq__), so dict operations are O(1) worst case since input cannot influence object addresses.
complexity.summary: Two-pass hashmap approach: first pass creates a new node for every original node and stores the old-to-new mapping in a dict, second pass wires up next and random pointers via the mapping.
